Description: 146 garment workers, mostly young immigrant women, died in a NYC factory fire; exit doors had been locked to prevent unauthorized breaks.
Structural_Note: Private employer imposed a physical risk the workforce could not exit; no external safety floor applied.

Authority: Colorado National Guard & Colorado Fuel & Iron Co. (its controlling family)
Description: Guardsmen and company guards attacked a striking miners' tent colony in Colorado; about 21 died, including two women and eleven children.
Structural_Note: State force deployed on behalf of a private authority against a non-consenting population.

Authority: Municipal officials and police in multiple US cities
Description: White mobs attacked Black communities across dozens of US cities; in many cases police participated or stood aside; hundreds killed.
Structural_Note: Public authority did not act to protect a population it was responsible for; private violence proceeded unchecked.

Authority: Tulsa city officials and deputized police
Description: A white mob, some deputized and armed by officials, destroyed the prosperous Black Greenwood district; estimates run to hundreds killed and thousands displaced.
Structural_Note: Public authority deputized and armed participants; the affected community had no protection from the authority meant to provide it.

Description: Tetraethyl lead was added to gasoline despite known toxicity; refinery workers died of lead poisoning in the 1920s and population-wide lead exposure persisted for decades until phase-out.
Structural_Note: A population-wide exposure was introduced without the consent of those exposed; once dispersed it was not reversible.

Authority: Commonwealth of Virginia / U.S. Supreme Court
Description: SCOTUS upheld compulsory sterilization of those deemed 'unfit'; the ruling enabled roughly 70,000 forced sterilizations across the states over subsequent decades.
Structural_Note: Judicial authorization for state control over the bodies of a non-consenting class; the ruling bound later cases.

Description: Federal researchers withheld treatment from hundreds of Black men with syphilis to study the disease's progression, continuing even after penicillin became standard; ran until 1972.
Structural_Note: Public research authority withheld an available treatment from non-consenting subjects, who could not see or stop the program.

Description: Federal troops used cavalry, tanks, and gas to clear WWI veterans and families demanding promised bonuses from encampments in Washington, DC.
Structural_Note: Military force used against citizens petitioning the government.

Description: About 120,000 people of Japanese descent, most U.S. citizens, were forcibly removed from their homes and held in camps without charge.
Structural_Note: Mass deprivation of liberty and property of a class defined by ancestry, without charge; later formally redressed by Congress.

Authority: U.S. Atomic Energy Commission and predecessors
Description: Government-sponsored researchers exposed uninformed patients, soldiers, and others to radiation, including plutonium injections, beginning in the 1940s.
Structural_Note: State conducted nonconsensual experiments; subjects could neither see nor stop them.

Authority: U.S. Steel (American Steel & Wire / zinc works)
Description: Industrial emissions trapped by a temperature inversion killed about 20 people and sickened thousands in Donora, Pennsylvania.
Structural_Note: Industrial emissions imposed acute harm on a host community with no means to halt them.

Description: The CIA secretly administered drugs including LSD to unwitting subjects and funded coercive experiments; ran until the 1970s, records largely destroyed.
Structural_Note: Covert state experimentation on non-consenting individuals; records were later destroyed, limiting external review.

Description: A federal campaign deported large numbers of Mexican nationals, with U.S. citizens of Mexican descent also detained and removed in the sweeps.
Structural_Note: Enforcement action removed individuals, including citizens, without individualized due process.

Description: The FBI ran covert programs to surveil, infiltrate, and disrupt civil-rights, anti-war, and political organizations, including unlawful tactics; exposed 1971.
Structural_Note: Domestic intelligence authority directed at lawful political activity.

Description: The heavily polluted Cuyahoga River in Cleveland, Ohio caught fire; one of several such fires, it became a national symbol of unregulated industrial discharge.
Structural_Note: A shared commons was degraded by industrial discharge whose cost fell on the public rather than the discharger.

Description: Guardsmen opened fire on a crowd during an anti-war protest at Kent State University in Ohio, killing four students and wounding nine.
Structural_Note: State force used against unarmed protesters, resulting in deaths.

Description: State forces retook Attica prison by force after a four-day uprising over conditions; 43 people died, most from state gunfire including hostages.
Structural_Note: State force in a custodial setting caused deaths among people in its own custody.

Event: Contamination and death of a plant worker raising safety concerns
Description: A nuclear-plant worker raising safety and contamination concerns was found contaminated with plutonium and died in a contested car crash; litigation found plant safety failures.
Structural_Note: A worker raising safety concerns was contaminated; litigation found facility safety failures.

Description: Thousands of tons of buried chemical waste contaminated a Niagara Falls, NY neighborhood and school, prompting a federal emergency and relocations.
Structural_Note: Waste disposed without disclosure left an unknowing community exposed; the contamination was not reversible.

Description: A partial reactor meltdown in Pennsylvania released radiation and exposed serious operator and regulatory shortcomings.
Structural_Note: Operator and regulator both fell short of the safeguards the surrounding population relied on.

Description: A gas leak at a Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, India killed thousands and injured hundreds of thousands; safety systems were inadequate.
Structural_Note: A U.S.-headquartered authority's operation imposed catastrophic risk on a foreign host population with no role in the decisions.

Description: Police dropped an explosive device on a row house occupied by the MOVE group, killing 11 people including 5 children and burning down 61 homes.
Structural_Note: Municipal authority used military-grade force in a residential neighborhood.

Authority: Thrift industry, federal regulators, and Congress
Description: Deregulation, lax supervision, and widespread fraud collapsed hundreds of thrifts; the taxpayer cleanup cost roughly $124 billion.
Structural_Note: Private risk-taking was followed by a public-funded backstop; the cost fell on taxpayers.

Description: A tanker ran aground in Prince William Sound, Alaska, spilling about 11 million gallons of crude and devastating the marine ecosystem.
Structural_Note: Coastal commons and dependent communities bore the cost of a private operator's failure.

Event: Police beating of a motorist during an arrest
Description: Officers were videotaped beating a man during an arrest; their later acquittal triggered widespread unrest.
Structural_Note: Documented use of force; internal review did not initially produce accountability.

Description: A federal siege in Idaho left a man's wife and son dead; subsequent reviews found rules-of-engagement and oversight failures.
Structural_Note: Federal force resulted in non-combatant deaths; later review found rules-of-engagement violations.

Description: A 51-day siege of the Branch Davidian compound in Texas ended in a fire; about 76 people died, including children.
Structural_Note: Escalation by federal authority preceded mass loss of life under circumstances still contested.

Description: Seven tobacco CEOs told Congress they did not believe nicotine was addictive; internal documents later showed the industry knew and concealed addiction and harm.
Structural_Note: Coordinated nondisclosure of known product risks; the public could not assess what it was not told.

Description: Purdue marketed OxyContin while downplaying addiction risk, helping ignite an opioid epidemic that has killed hundreds of thousands.
Structural_Note: Product risks were systematically misrepresented to prescribers and the public.

Description: The law repealed Depression-era separations between commercial and investment banking, later cited as a contributor to the 2008 crisis.
Structural_Note: A statutory separation between commercial and investment banking was removed, recombining activities previously kept apart.

Description: Accounting fraud hid massive losses; the firm's collapse wiped out employee retirement savings and destroyed its auditor.
Structural_Note: Falsified accounting, later adjudicated, shifted concealed risk onto employees and investors.

Description: Published photographs documented torture and humiliation of detainees by U.S. personnel at a prison in Iraq.
Structural_Note: Custodial authority abused detainees within its power, outside legal limits.

Authority: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers / FEMA
Description: Engineered flood-protection systems failed during Katrina, flooding New Orleans; about 1,800 died and the federal response was widely judged inadequate.
Structural_Note: Engineered flood protection and the emergency response both fell short for the population relying on them.

Event: Purdue pleads guilty to OxyContin misbranding
Description: The company and executives admitted misleading regulators, doctors, and patients about OxyContin's addiction risk; marketing continued afterward.
Structural_Note: Company admitted misbranding; marketing continued afterward.

Authority: Major banks; SEC and Federal Reserve oversight
Description: Predatory lending and opaque securities triggered the worst crash since the 1930s; millions lost homes and jobs while large institutions were bailed out.
Structural_Note: Concentrated private risk was realized as broad public loss; large institutions received public support.

Authority: A Ponzi-scheme operator; SEC supervisory failure
Description: A roughly $65 billion Ponzi scheme collapsed; the SEC had received and dismissed credible warnings for years.
Structural_Note: The regulator received specific, repeated warnings and did not act on them.

Description: An explosion at a West Virginia coal mine killed 29 workers; investigators cited systematic safety violations and a culture of concealment.
Structural_Note: Investigators cited systematic safety violations and falsified records preceding worker deaths.

Description: A blowout killed 11 workers and released about 4 million barrels of oil into the Gulf of Mexico, the largest marine oil spill in U.S. history.
Structural_Note: Safety shortcuts preceded a blowout causing worker deaths and large-scale, hard-to-reverse ecological harm.

Description: Leaked documents revealed bulk collection of Americans' phone and internet records, much of it later found to lack adequate legal basis.
Structural_Note: Bulk collection of the general population's records, much later found to lack adequate legal basis.

Description: GM recalled millions of cars over a defect linked to at least 124 deaths that the company had known about for roughly a decade.
Structural_Note: A known defect linked to deaths went undisclosed for years before recall.

Authority: State of Michigan (emergency managers) / MDEQ / EPA
Description: A state-directed switch in water source, without corrosion control, exposed Flint residents to lead and bacteria; officials downplayed the danger.
Structural_Note: A state-directed water-source change exposed residents to lead; official responses to early warnings were delayed.

Description: VW installed software that detected emissions tests and reduced emissions controls in normal driving on millions of cars, so they emitted far more pollution than reported; the company later pleaded guilty in US federal court.
Structural_Note: Software designed to defeat emissions tests increased pollution beyond reported levels; later adjudicated.

Description: Employees opened millions of accounts without customers' authorization to meet sales quotas, harming some customers' credit and finances; the company later paid settlements to federal regulators.
Structural_Note: Sales-quota pressure resulted in millions of unauthorized customer accounts.

Description: A breach exposed sensitive personal data of about 147 million people; the company had failed to patch a known vulnerability.
Structural_Note: A custodian of data collected without the subjects' consent left a known vulnerability unpatched; ~147M people were exposed.

Authority: Department of Homeland Security / Department of Justice
Description: A policy of prosecuting border crossers led to thousands of children being separated from parents, many without adequate tracking to reunite them.
Structural_Note: Families were separated without a reliable mechanism to reunite them; the harm was difficult to reverse.

Description: A wildfire ignited by aging utility equipment destroyed the town of Paradise, California and killed 85 people; the utility later pleaded guilty.
Structural_Note: Aging utility equipment ignited a fatal wildfire; the utility later pleaded guilty.

Description: Two crashes tied to flawed flight-control software killed 346 people; reviews found Boeing concealed information and the FAA delegated too much oversight to Boeing.
Structural_Note: Reviews found the safety regulator had delegated oversight to the firm it was meant to check.

Description: A train carrying hazardous chemicals derailed in East Palestine, Ohio; a controlled burn of vinyl chloride contaminated air, soil, and water and forced evacuations.
Structural_Note: Hazardous material moved through a community became contamination the community had not consented to.

Description: Poor interest-rate risk management triggered the second-largest U.S. bank failure; supervisors had flagged but not resolved the weaknesses.
Structural_Note: Interest-rate risk and supervisory gaps preceded the failure, affecting depositors and the wider system.

Description: A door plug blew out mid-flight; investigators found missing bolts and recurring quality-control failures in Boeing's production.
Structural_Note: Recurring production-quality failures, after earlier crashes, again exposed the flying public to risk.
